newsitem.title: ITALY: Earthquake jolts central Italy's Umbrian region.
newsitem.headline: Earthquake jolts central Italy's Umbrian region.

text.p: An earthquake measuring 4.5 on the Richter scale rocked most of the central Italian region of Umbria on Monday, civil defence officials said.
There were no early reports of serious damage or injuries, but thousands of people ran out of their homes in panic.
The quake measured 4.5 on the Richter scale and 7.0 on the Mercalli scale, a civil protection official said.
Earthquakes measuring between four and five on the Richter scale can cause heavy damage in populated areas.
The earthquake was believed to be centred in the Martani mountains, where police said residents had reported falling masonry and damage to rural buildings.
The quake hit at about 3.50 p.m. (1350 GMT). It was felt in the Umbrian cities of Terni, Perugia and Orvieto and towns including Todi, Spoleto and Assisi, the birthplace of St Francis.
It was also felt as far south as the northern part of Lazio, the region around Rome.
